_note: Monte Carlo companion for the transimpedance stage. Contributes fragments only;
the master file and the corner fragments come from anatop_tb_tia.json.
block is TiaAmpMC, NOT TiaAmp -- the block name keys data/raw/corners_<Block>.json
and data/extract_<Block>.ocn, which the configs would otherwise clobber.
The two tests are NOT two Maestro tests. Maestro writes one mcdata per test
containing every design point pooled, so the 35k and 560k gain taps land in one
file and maestro2tex would average them together into nonsense. scratchpad/
split_mc.py splits them into TiaFbTB35k__mc.csv / TiaFbTB560k__mc.csv and drops
the 48 of 400 samples that did not converge. Render with --no-extract; there is
no live run to extract from and the CSVs are self-describing.
PUBLISHABLE OUTPUTS ONLY. Every DC-sweep-derived output (gain_err, inl_lsb,
tue_lsb, f3db, x_src_lim) is deliberately absent: they degrade on the same
samples as the 48 non-converged ones and are under investigation. Do not add

figures.caption: Transimpedance loop phase margin at maximum gain. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling, $N = 179$. Minimum \SI{46.6}{\degree} against a \SI{45}{\degree} criterion. Reported as percentiles and extreme sample; the distribution is right-skewed.

Closed-loop gain peaking at maximum gain, conditions as Figure~\ref{fig:tia-mc-pm560k}. \SI{87.7}{\percent} of samples below \SI{2}{\decibel}, maximum \SI{2.61}{\decibel}. At $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$ the response is monotonic and peaking is \SI{0}{\decibel} on every sample.

Input offset at maximum gain, conditions as Figure~\ref{fig:tia-mc-pm560k}. \(\sigma = \SI{7.09}{\milli\volt}\); \SI{54.7}{\percent} of samples within \(\pm\SI{5}{\milli\volt}\), \SI{9.0}{\percent} over four channels. At $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$, \(\sigma = \SI{4.70}{\milli\volt}\) and \SI{74.0}{\percent}.

tables.caption: Monte Carlo stability at minimum gain, $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$. \textbf{Process and mismatch} (\texttt{castalia\_pm\_25}), \SI{37}{\celsius}, 200 samples, seed 12345, LDS sampling, $C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$, electrode \texttt{randles\_cell} with $R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$. $N$ is the number of samples whose DC operating point lies in the linear range of Equation~(\ref{eq:tia-transfer}); see Section~\ref{sss:tia-mc}. \(\sigma\) combines process and mismatch and is not comparable with a mismatch-only \(\sigma\).
Monte Carlo stability at maximum gain, $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$, conditions otherwise as Table~\ref{tab:tia-mc-stab35k}.

Monte Carlo input offset and input-referred current noise at maximum gain, conditions as Table~\ref{tab:tia-mc-stab560k}. The offset distribution is close to Gaussian; mean \(\pm\,3\sigma\) is given for it and not for the skewed stability quantities. At $R_f = \SI{35}{\kilo\ohm}$, \(\sigma = \SI{4.70}{\milli\volt}\) and \SI{74.0}{\percent} of samples lie within \(\pm\SI{5}{\milli\volt}\). The four-channel column assumes independent channels.
